settings.eyebrow: VoiceSieve by Braivex · Voice agents for commerce
settings.heading: VoiceSieve
settings.lede: Phone calls, answered and made from what your best people already said. VoiceSieve mines your recorded calls into a knowledge base and a house style, answers inbound calls live against your order system, and calls lapsed customers back — declaring itself an AI in its first sentence, every call.
settings.metric: Specified end to end — nine architecture decisions, eight research reports; product build starts after sign-off

settings.label: Mine · your calls become the knowledge base
settings.value: Historical recordings for the agents you name are transcribed, speaker-separated and redacted for personal data, then distilled into structured notes, a searchable knowledge base and a house style guide. Both agents below speak from it.

settings.label: Inbound · answers from the order system
settings.value: The top intent on a commerce line is “where is my order?”. VoiceSieve resolves it live against Shopify — dispatch, carrier, tracking, expected date — and says nothing the data does not support. No date in the record, no date spoken.

settings.label: Outbound · win-back, one call at a time
settings.value: Works a list of lapsed customers scored on recency, frequency and value, inside a calling window you set. Objection handling is mined from the real calls that won customers back. Offers come only from an approved matrix.

settings.label: Disclosure, first sentence
settings.value: The agent says it is an AI assistant before any question is asked and before any caller data is requested, with the recording notice in the same breath. Asked “are you a robot?”, it answers plainly and at once.

settings.label: Hands off when it does not know
settings.value: If the answer is not in an authoritative source — the order system, the offer matrix, an approved policy — the agent says so and offers a callback or a transfer to a person, with the notes attached. It never guesses.

settings.label: Open-source-first, no per-minute markup
settings.value: Built on an open voice runtime and self-hosted telephony, with licences checked for the model weights and not only the code. The aim is platform-class quality without the platform's per-minute fee.

settings.heading: Three components. One voice, learnt from yours.
settings.lede: Designed for a wholesale commerce business whose phone still rings — and whose customers deserve an honest answer when it does.

settings.label: Invent a fact
settings.value: No product name, price, discount, stock level, lead time, delivery date or policy unless it came from an authoritative source on that turn.

settings.label: Invent scarcity or urgency
settings.value: Unless the offer matrix carries that fact with a real date.

settings.label: Talk about competitors
settings.value: No claims about their prices, quality or reliability.

settings.label: Improvise an offer
settings.value: The agent cannot combine, extend or increase an offer, and cannot match a figure a caller says they were quoted.

settings.label: Push past a no
settings.value: An explicit refusal ends persuasion for that call, and is recorded.

settings.label: Admit liability or promise compensation
settings.value: It may apologise for the experience. It may not accept fault or promise a refund, credit or replacement — that is a person's decision.

settings.heading: What it will never say.
settings.lede: Persuasive is allowed. Dishonest is not — and no caller, campaign target or instruction can soften that.

settings.a: Not yet. The research and the full specification are complete — the stack, the conversation design, the data model, the compliance obligations and the evaluation plan. Product build starts after sign-off. Join the waitlist to be onboarded first.

settings.q: Will callers know they are talking to an AI?
settings.a: Yes, in the first sentence, before any question is asked — with the recording notice in the same opening. Asked directly, it says so again, plainly.

settings.q: Can it invent an offer to close a sale?
settings.a: No. Offers come only from an approved matrix. It cannot combine, extend or increase one, and it cannot match a figure a caller claims to have been quoted. A no ends the pitch.

settings.q: What happens when it does not know?
settings.a: It says so and offers a callback or a transfer to a person, with its notes attached. It does not guess and does not give hedged half-answers.
